data.gender_notes: Muharrem is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Muharram' which means 'sacred, inviolable, or invincible'. This name is commonly used in the Islamic world, particularly during the month of Muharram in commemoration of Imam Hussein's martyrdom. The name Muharrem carries the meaning “Sacred, Invincible” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muharrem usually hope their child will grow to embody sacred, invincible and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muharrem total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar, and it holds special significance in Islamic culture. During this month, many Muslims around the world observe various rituals and practices in remembrance of Imam Hussein, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and his companions who were martyred in the Battle of Karbala in 680 AD. The events of this battle are reenacted through various mourning ceremonies, including the symbolic flagellation processions called "Majlis" and "Taziya," and communal gatherings for reciting historical and poetic accounts of the tragedy.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Muharram" holds a deep spiritual significance for Muslims, as it serves to remind them of the sacrifices made by Imam Hussein and his companions in the pursuit of truth, justice, and selflessness. This month and the associated rituals and practices encourage Muslims to reflect upon the virtues of patience, sacrifice, and devotion, traits that are encouraged in the Islamic faith. Furthermore, it serves to teach the value of expressing mourning through communal gatherings and prayers, fostering a sense of solidarity and mutual support within the Muslim community.

historical_references.reference: The month of Muharram is the second month of the Islamic calendar and is considered sacred as it marks the anniversary of the emigration of Prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD. This event is known as the Hijra and marks the beginning of the Islamic era.
historical_references.context: Prophet Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina

historical_references.reference: The Battle of Karbala took place in the plain of Karbala, in present-day Iraq, in October or November 680 AD during the first Islamic civil war. The battle was between the forces of Umar ibn Al-Khattab's Umayyad Caliphate, led by Umar ibn Sa'ad, and the forces of Ali ibn Husain, who was the fourth caliph and grandson of Prophet Muhammad. Muharram is significant in Shia Islam as it marks the day when Imam Husain and his companions were martyred in this battle, leading to the observance of Ashura as a day of mourning and commemoration.
historical_references.context: Battle of Karbala and martyrdom of Imam Husain

trends: Muharram is the first month in the Islamic calendar and is considered sacred as it marks the beginning of the new year.
It is also the month when the Prophet Muhammad and his companions were forced to leave Mecca and migrate to Medina in 622 AD.
Muharram is a time of reflection, repentance, and charitable giving for Muslims around the world.

modern_usage.modern_context: Despite being a significant religious occasion, Muharram is also a time for social media engagement and online discourse among Muslims worldwide. The hashtags #Muharram, #Ashura, #RemembranceOfThemartyrs, #Muharram2023, and #Ashura2023 are commonly used on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram to share information, inspirational quotes, and personal experiences related to the month. The online community also allows people to connect with others and participate in virtual events, such as live recitations of historical and religious texts, which may not be accessible to everyone physically.
